title: Excel on Windows and Mac: Copilot Agent Mode (Edit with Copilot) builds and edits workbooks, with a choice of model
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing requirement and documented controls are supported. Minor corrections should acknowledge Microsoft's differing regional Claude-default guidance, cite the source confirming the editing default, and complete the shortened governance path.

claims.claim: Agent Mode builds and edits Excel workbooks through multi-step workflows on Windows and Mac.
claims.quote: Agent Mode is releasing to Copilot in Excel on Windows and Mac enabling users to build and edit workbooks with Copilot using multi-step workflows.

claims.claim: Agent Mode is now called Edit with Copilot.
claims.quote: Edit with Copilot in Excel to enhance your productivity (formerly Agent Mode)

claims.claim: The March 10, 2026 release notes associate Edit with Copilot in Excel with roadmap items 542182 and 527835.
claims.quote:
March 10, 2026
Updates released between February 24, 2026, March 10, 2026
### Excel
- **Edit with Copilot in Excel to enhance your productivity (formerly Agent Mode)** [Windows, Web, Mac]
**Roadmap IDs:** 542182, 527835

claims.claim: The release notes list Windows, Web and Mac for Edit with Copilot in Excel.
claims.quote: **Edit with Copilot in Excel to enhance your productivity (formerly Agent Mode)** [Windows, Web, Mac]

claims.claim: Copilot edits workbooks through chat using tables, charts, PivotTables and formulas.
claims.quote: Edit with Copilot in Excel to build and change workbooks, using Excel tools like tables, charts, PivotTables, and formulas to complete complex data tasks faster.

claims.claim: The release notes direct users without the Let's edit together message to the tools menu and Edit with Copilot.
claims.quote:
Open Copilot chat in Excel and see "Let's edit together" welcome message.
If you don't see the message, then go to the tools menu and select "Edit with Copilot".

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Edit with Copilot can execute Python code and output results directly into the workbook.
claims.quote: Edit with Copilot helps you work with Python in Excel by executing Python code for advanced analysis, automation, and data transformation with results outputted directly in your workbook.

claims.claim: The Python capability was announced in the August 2026 release notes.
claims.quote:
August 25, 2026
Updates released between August 11, 2026, and August 25, 2026.
### Excel
**Use Python when Editing with Copilot in Excel** [Windows, Mac, Web]

claims.claim: Microsoft says existing security and execution controls continue to manage how Python code runs.
claims.quote: Existing security and execution controls continue to help manage how code runs.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Users can select Claude in Edit with Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps when provider access permits it.
claims.quote: In capabilities such as Edit with Copilot in Microsoft 365 apps or Researcher, users can select **Claude**.

claims.claim: Claude models are on by default for most commercial-cloud customers outside the EU, EFTA and UK.
claims.quote: Microsoft enables Claude models on by default for most customers in commercial cloud (excluding EU/EFTA and UK).

claims.claim: Microsoft's general Anthropic page says the EU, EFTA and UK default is No users.
claims.quote: the default is set to **No users**. These regions include the European Union (EU), the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), and the United Kingdom (UK).
claims.fix: After the regional-default statement, add: 'However, Microsoft's apps-specific guidance says the apps-only setting is enabled by default for EU, EFTA and UK tenants created after March 25, 2026; check the actual tenant setting.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/copilot-anthropic-apps, which states: 'This setting is enabled by default for tenants in the EU, EFTA, and UK that were created after March 25, 2026.'

claims.claim: Microsoft Product Terms and DPA apply to Claude use except models labelled Anthropic models with Data Retention.
claims.quote: Unless models are labeled "Anthropic models with Data Retention," the Microsoft Product Terms and Microsoft Data Protection Addendum (DPA) apply to the use of Claude models from Anthropic through Microsoft's enterprise Online Services.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Anthropic operates the Claude models as a Microsoft subprocessor in the documented subprocessor experience.
claims.quote:
Anthropic has onboarded as a Microsoft subprocessor.
Claude models have built-in safeguards, instantiated and operated by Anthropic, to detect illegal content.

claims.claim: Claude processing for Copilot in Excel, PowerPoint and Word occurs outside the EU Data Boundary.
claims.quote: When Claude models from Anthropic are used in Copilot experiences in Excel, PowerPoint, or Word, data processing for these models occurs outside of the EU Data Boundary.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Claude models are coming into the EU Data Boundary starting in December 2026.
claims.quote: Claude models from Anthropic are coming into the EU Data Boundary starting in December 2026.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[1].note; Governance guidance
claims.claim: On December 9, 2026, EU, EFTA and UK tenants with All users for Microsoft 365 apps only selected move to All users.
claims.quote:
Starting on December 9, 2026, the following setting changes are taking effect:
If the **All users for Microsoft 365 apps only** option is currently selected, the selection will change to the **All users** option.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: EU, EFTA and UK tenants with no selection also move to All users on December 9, 2026.
claims.quote: If you haven't previously made any selection, your selection will change to **All users**.

claims.claim: Explicit No users or specific-user/group selections avoid the automatic widening to All users.
claims.quote:
If you've selected any other option, including **No users**, your selection won't change.
Specific users and groups for all Copilot and generative AI experiences | Specific users and groups

claims.claim: Moving from apps-only to All users expands Claude access beyond Excel, PowerPoint and Word.
claims.quote: If you want to make Claude models available to your users beyond just Copilot experiences in Microsoft 365 apps, select **All users**, or specify users and groups, and then select **Save**.

claims.claim: AI Administrator or Global Administrator is required to change the Anthropic setting.
claims.quote: You must be a member of the AI Administrator or Global Administrator role to perform this task.

claims.claim: Anthropic user/group assignments operate at provider level across Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: These assignments are applied at the provider level and enforced across Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Studio experiences. When access is limited by user or group membership, only the assigned users can use Copilot features or agents that rely on that AI provider.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[3].governs; Governance guidance
claims.claim: BlockContentAnalysisServices on a sensitivity label excludes labelled workbook content from Copilot in the named Office apps.
claims.quote: Although content with the configured sensitivity label will be excluded from Microsoft 365 Copilot in the named Office apps, the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios.

claims.claim: The labelled content remains available to Copilot in other scenarios, including Teams and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: the content remains available to Microsoft 365 Copilot for other scenarios. For example, in Teams, and in Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The label setting affects other services, including automatic and recommended labelling.
claims.quote: when it's set, it means that some services won't work as designed, such as data loss prevention policy tips for Outlook, automatic and recommended labeling, and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Editing is part of the regular Copilot in Excel experience for eligible users, supporting defaultState on.
claims.quote: Copilot in Excel offers three modes: edit, plan, or chat. By default, Copilot in Excel opens in edit mode.
claims.fix: Add https://support.microsoft.com/topic/a2fd6fe4-97ac-416b-b89a-22f4d1357c7a to sources as 'Get started with Copilot in Excel'; it explicitly confirms the editing default. Keep defaultState as on.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Scope: Admin roles; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Licences can be assigned at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote:
go to the **Users** > Active users page.
Select the row of the user ...
In the right pane, select **Licenses and Apps**.
Expand the **Licenses** section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses SkuId and an empty RemoveLicenses array assigns the selected user licence.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: The Anthropic user-scope path follows Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences.
claims.quote:
select **Copilot** > **Settings** > **View all**.
Select **AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors**.
under **Available subprocessors for your organization**, select **Anthropic**
Under **Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences**

claims.claim: No API or PowerShell operation for the Anthropic provider user-scope setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Anthropic subprocessor settings Microsoft Graph API PowerShell configure users'; 'Anthropic API settings'. Read connect-to-ai-subprocessor, copilot-ai-provider-user-sec-group-access and copilotPolicySetting; no operation for this setting found.

claims.claim: The analyze-content policy is under Group Policy Management > User Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Office 2016 > Privacy > Trust Center.
claims.quote:
all these policy settings are located under User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center.
Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content

claims.claim: Setting UserContentDisabled to 2 disables the analyze-content connected-experiences policy.
claims.quote: | Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled  2=Disabled |

claims.claim: Disabling connected experiences that analyze content removes Copilot features in Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word, not just Excel editing.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
- Excel
- OneNote
- Outlook
- PowerPoint
- Word

claims.claim: The connected-experiences policies can also be implemented through Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: These policy settings can be implemented by using either Group Policy or Cloud Policy.

claims.claim: The BlockContentAnalysisServices label configuration has no Microsoft Purview portal UI.
claims.quote: Searched: 'BlockContentAnalysisServices portal'. Read sensitivity-labels-office-apps, Prevent connected experiences that analyze content: 'This configuration isn't available in the Microsoft Purview portal.' It directs administrators to PowerShell.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label GUID> -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"} configures the label restriction.
claims.quote: Set-Label -Identity "8faca7b8-8d20-48a3-8ea2-0f96310a848e" -AdvancedSettings @{BlockContentAnalysisServices="True"}

claims.where: controls[4].ui; controls[4].api; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No documented UI or API switch disables Edit with Copilot in Excel alone while retaining other Copilot features.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edit with Copilot disable policy'; 'Edit with Copilot turn off Excel administrator'; 'Copilot Excel Agent Mode admin disable policy specific editing'. Read privacy controls, Copilot privacy, Graph policy settings and Excel getting-started pages; no editing-only switch found.

claims.claim: The Graph copilotPolicySetting supported-settings list contains neither Anthropic nor Edit with Copilot.
claims.quote: Searched: Anthropic and Edit with Copilot in the complete copilotPolicySetting reference; supported IDs are copilotchatpinning, blockaccesstoopenfiles, imagegeneration, allowwebsearch and allowinadmincenters. Neither requested setting appears.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, first bullet
claims.claim: The shortened Anthropic route reaches the AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors page.
claims.quote:
Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center and select **Copilot** > **Settings** > **View all**.
Select **AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors**.
claims.fix: Complete the first governance bullet's route as 'Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > AI providers operating as Microsoft subprocessors > Available subprocessors for your organization > Anthropic > Choose who can access Anthropic models for Copilot and generative AI experiences', matching controls[1].ui.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents Set-Label or New-Label in Security & Compliance PowerShell for the BlockContentAnalysisServices advanced setting.
claims.quote: You must use the PowerShell advanced setting *BlockContentAnalysisServices* with the Set-Label or New-Label cmdlet after you've connected to Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Excel's Show Changes pane provides on-card attribution for Copilot edits.
claims.quote: Now, the pane includes on-card attribution showing when Copilot made edits or suggestions. This transparency helps users track AI contributions alongside manual changes.

claims.claim: Copilot chat responses link to changed sheets, tables and ranges.
claims.quote: In Copilot in Excel, the response contains links to highlight where changes are made in your workbook. Navigate directly to new sheets, tables, ranges, and objects like charts and shapes.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes the workbook-editing capabilities formerly called Agent Mode as part of the regular Copilot in Excel experience.
claims.quote: The workbook-editing capabilities previously called *Agent Mode* are now part of the regular Copilot in Excel experience.
